summary: The investigation could not definitively identify a root cause; while the leading hypothesis (a bug in order-service v2.15.2 causing exchange-gateway timeouts) has the highest confidence, it lacks direct evidence. The observed simultaneous spikes in exchange-gateway latency and error rate (F17, F18) and the timing of order-service errors (F8, F9, F11) are consistent with multiple plausible causes. Further data collection is required to discriminate between a deployment bug, exchange-gateway degradation, or a network issue.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bug introduced in order-service v2.15.2 causing exchange-gateway timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The deployment of order-service version v2.15.2 introduced a code defect that sends malformed or delayed requests to exchange-gateway, which responds with 504 Gateway Timeout, leading to a surge in order-service error rate.

causal_chain.claim: code defect causes exchange-gateway calls to fail with 504
order-service error rate spikes to ~30% and latency >5s

assumptions: The code change in v2.15.2 modifies the request to exchange-gateway in a way that triggers timeouts.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Exchange-gateway degradation causing order-service timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A performance degradation or outage in the exchange-gateway service caused it to return 504 Gateway Timeout for placeOrder calls, which manifested as a high error rate in order-service.

causal_chain.claim: exchange-gateway experiences latency or failure resulting in 504 responses
order-service error rate spikes to ~30% and latency >5s

assumptions: The exchange-gateway degradation began around 11:00 UTC, coincident with the observed error spike.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Network connectivity issue between order-service and exchange-gateway
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A network partition or increased packet loss between order-service and exchange-gateway caused HTTP requests to time out, resulting in 504 errors and elevated order-service failure rates.

causal_chain.claim: Network issues (latency, loss) affect traffic to exchange-gateway
order-service receives 504 Gateway Timeout from exchange-gateway
order-service error rate spikes to ~30% and latency >5s

assumptions: Network metrics would show degradation starting around 11:00 UTC.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm rollback of order-service v2.15.2 is complete and monitor for error_rate reduction
recommended_actions.rationale: Rollback removes the only recent code change; if the bug is the cause, error metrics should improve.

recommended_actions.action: Collect detailed code diff for v2.15.2, focusing on request payload, timeout settings, and retry logic for exchange-gateway client
recommended_actions.rationale: Direct evidence is needed to confirm or refute H1's assumption that the new header/retry logic triggers timeouts.

recommended_actions.action: Obtain exchange-gateway internal metrics (CPU, memory, thread pools) and logs around 11:00 UTC
recommended_actions.rationale: If exchange-gateway itself degraded, its own resource usage or error logs would show anomalies, supporting H2.

recommended_actions.action: Gather network path health data (packet loss, latency, jitter) between order-service and exchange-gateway for the incident window
recommended_actions.rationale: Network degradation would manifest in packet loss or increased RTT, addressing the gap for H3.

recommended_actions.action: Implement monitoring for packet loss and connection health for all critical service-to-service links
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents future blind spots similar to the current data gaps.

recommended_actions.action: Add automated regression tests that validate exchange-gateway request format and timeout behavior after deployments
recommended_actions.rationale: Ensures future code changes that affect downstream calls are caught before release.

data_gaps: Missing memory usage and DB connection pool metrics for order-service (cannot assess resource pressure).
No detailed code diff or configuration values for the exchange-gateway client in v2.15.2 (cannot confirm payload or timeout changes).
No packet loss or other network health metrics for the order-service ↔ exchange-gateway path (cannot evaluate network hypothesis).
No internal metrics or logs from exchange-gateway to determine if it experienced its own degradation.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: If the code diff shows that the Idempotency-Key header or retry logic modifies request timing or size in a way that triggers exchange-gateway timeouts, H1 would become strongly supported.
If exchange-gateway internal logs reveal a spike in resource usage, thread pool exhaustion, or a separate failure at 11:00 UTC, H2 would be confirmed.
If network telemetry shows a sudden increase in packet loss or latency between the two services at the incident onset, H3 would be validated.

findings.statement: The first error log from order-service appears at 2026-03-17T11:02:45Z.
All early errors share the signature "exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)" indicating the placeOrder endpoint is failing.

findings.statement: The first error log from exchange-gateway for the placeOrder endpoint appears at 2026-03-17T11:01:25Z.
All 42 error entries in the window share the same pattern "upstream connect timeout after <n>ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder".
exchange-gateway p99 latency (ms) was stable around 125‑135 ms before 11:00 UTC, then jumped to 3514 ms (avg) at 11:00 UTC and stayed above 5 s for the remainder of the window.
exchange-gateway error_rate (HTTP 5xx %) was ~0.2 % before 11:00 UTC, spiked to 29.15 % (avg) at 11:00 UTC and remained in the 40‑47 % range thereafter.
The latency and error_rate spikes align with the first observed timeout log (11:01:25Z), indicating the degradation began just after 11:00 UTC.
